glosses: A short report, especially one released through official channels to be immediately broadcast or publicized.

examples.text: A company bulletin announced changes to the policy.

glosses: A time-sensitive news item or short news report.

examples.text: The evening news bulletin reported on the earthquake.

glosses: A short printed publication, especially one produced regularly by an organization.
To announce (something) by means of such a report or publication.

examples.text: to bulletin an employment vacancy

glosses: Introduces a fact (presumed to be obvious) of which the person addressed is ostensibly not aware.

translations.source_sense_description: ein Informationsblatt, das öffentlich zur Schau gehängt wird

glosses: The act of observing; perception.

examples.text: He took no notice of the changes, and went on as though nothing had happened.

Athelstan Arundel walked home[…], foaming and raging. […] He walked the whole way, walking through crowds, and under the noses of dray-horses, carriage-horses, and cart-horses, without taking the least notice of them.
How ready is envy to mingle with the notices which we take of other persons?

glosses: A written or printed announcement.

examples.text: Shall we post a notice about the new policy?
A notice was attached to the building reminding the residents about the five hour water shortage that was happening today.
I always read the death notices in the paper.

glosses: A formal notification or warning.

examples.text: The sidewalk adjacent to the damaged bridge stonework shall be closed until further notice.

glosses: Advance notification of termination of employment, given by an employer to an employee or vice versa.

examples.text: I gave her her mandatory two weeks' notice and sacked her.
I can't work here any longer. I'm giving notice.

glosses: A published critical review of a play or the like.

examples.text: The first-night audience, yes. The first-night reviewers, not exactly. The notices have so far been mixed, only The Financial Times having delivered itself of an unequivocal rave.

glosses: Prior notification.

examples.text: I don't mind if you want to change the venue; just give me some notice first, OK?
I have been with your father and given him notice that the Duke of Cornwall and Regan his duchess will be here with him this night.

glosses: Attention; respectful treatment; civility.
To remark upon; to mention.

examples.text: Numberless are the arguments […] that men have used morally and physically, to degrade the sex. I must notice a few.

glosses: To become aware of; to observe.

examples.text: Did you notice the flowers in her yard?
So you punched out a window for ventilation. Was that before or after you noticed you were standing in a lake of gasoline?

[The researchers] noticed many of their pieces of [plastic marine] debris sported surface pits around two microns across. Such pits are about the size of a bacterial cell. Closer examination showed that some of these pits did, indeed, contain bacteria, […].

glosses: To lavish attention upon; to treat (someone) favourably.

examples.text: She would notice her; she would improve her; she would detach her from her bad acquaintance, and introduce her into good society; she would form her opinions and her manners.

glosses: To be noticeable; to show.

examples.text: The blackness didn't notice so much when she was born; but it's unmistakeable now.

glosses: A sheet of paper or cardboard with a written or printed announcement on one side for display in a public place.

examples.text: Especially from Mr. Borthrop Trumbull, a distinguished bachelor and auctioneer of those parts, much concerned in the sale of land and cattle: a public character, indeed, whose name was seen on widely distributed placards, and who might reasonably be sorry for those who did not know of him.
He brought out the placard, which was quite a work of art. It was nearly two feet long, printed on calendered paper, with a selection of colors so bright that they shone even in the moonlight.
While her husband read the placards pasted on the brick announcing the hours at which certain ships would sail for Scotland, Mrs. Ambrose did her best to find information.

Towards the end of August, the Southern Railway decided to adopt a novel form of publicity to popularise the services. Sandwich board men were employed at Charing Cross and Cannon Street to display placards, and distribute leaflet timetables, calling attention to the vacant seats on the services via Nunhead.

glosses: A public proclamation; a manifesto or edict issued by authority.

examples.text: All placards or edicts are published in his name.

glosses: Permission given by authority; a license.

glosses: An extra plate on the lower part of the breastplate or backplate of armour.

examples.text: The inner walls of the church were placarded with large mural tablets of copper, bearing engraved inscriptions celebrating the merits of old Heilbronn worthies of two or three centuries ago, […]

glosses: Feuille souple ou rigide affichant un message, ou une image, imprimé ou écrit que l’on applique contre les murs pour donner connaissance au public de quelque chose.

examples.text: Elle collectionne aussi toutes les plaques officielles des rues, et à chaque instant un généreux donateur arrive, apportant des panonceaux ou des affiches.

[…], je lis avec effarement, à plusieurs encoignures, des affiches enluminées […]. « Engagez-vous dans l’armée coloniale ! » s’écrie l’autre, toute enluminée de perroquets, toute rehaussée de nudités affriolantes.
[…], elle considéra, sans bouger, une affiche qui représentait une gitane devant un paysage andalou.

Les petits chevaux des Cosaques escaladent les amas de décombres, entre des lambeaux de murs placardés d’affiches portant la dernière proclamation de Gœbbels : « Tout Allemand doit défendre sa capitale. Les hordes rouges seront arrêtées. »
Le détournement d’affiche par les militants adverses, le plus souvent par graffiti ou bombage, constitue une pratique aussi ancienne que l’affiche politique elle-même.

glosses: Ensemble des artistes ou spectacles programmés dans un lieu ou lors d’un événement culturel.

examples.text: La Cantatrice chauve est à l’affiche du théâtre de la Huchette depuis 1957.
Ce festival a une affiche éclectique.

glosses: Action d'afficher (au sens figuré).

examples.text: Il échappe au mépris des autres par l´affiche du mépris qu'il fait de lui-même.
